steps.name: Load, QC-align counts/metadata/signature and normalize counts
caveats: counts.csv is described as 12000 x 121 while metadata.csv is 120 x 4 — one row/column is not a sample; identify and document which before merging, do not assume alignment by position
Salmon gene counts may need integer rounding before DESeq2 ingestion if they carry fractional values from transcript-length aggregation
If gene identifiers in counts.csv are not HGNC symbols, use the human UniProt ID mapping or org.Hs.eg.db to resolve the 20 signature gene symbols before subsetting
steps.question: Do the 121-sample counts.csv, 120-sample metadata.csv, and 20-gene signature_genes.csv align on sample identifiers and gene symbols, and what does a DESeq2 size-factor + VST normalization of the raw Salmon gene counts look like for this cohort?
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs in counts.csv (minus any gene-ID column) are matched 1:1 against metadata.csv rows; any mismatch (121 vs 120) is resolved and reported explicitly (e.g., one column is a gene identifier, not a sample)
All 20 signature genes are located in the count matrix by symbol (or via an ID mapping if counts are Ensembl-indexed); genes not found are reported by name, not silently dropped
DESeq2 is run only for size-factor estimation and variance-stabilizing transformation (VST) — no differential expression test is performed
Output is a VST-normalized expression matrix (genes x samples) and a merged sample-level table joining metadata (condition, time, event) with sample IDs, saved for downstream steps

steps.name: Compute unweighted 20-gene signature score per sample
caveats: If any signature genes are near-zero-count/low-expression across the cohort, flag them rather than silently including a noisy z-score in the composite
Do not use any outcome information (time/event) when constructing the score — the score must be computed independent of the survival outcome to avoid circularity
steps.question: What is each sample's composite score for the pre-specified 20-gene signature, given that no per-gene weights are provided?
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 20 signature genes' VST-normalized expression is z-scored across the 121 samples
A single per-sample signature score is computed as the unweighted mean of the 20 per-gene z-scores (documented explicitly as the scoring choice, since the signature file carries no weights)
Output is a sample-level table with sample ID, signature_score, condition (case/control), time, and event, ready for survival modeling
Distribution of the score is reported (histogram/summary stats) and checked for outliers or genes dominating the score due to low expression/high variance

steps.name: Multivariable Cox model: signature score adjusted for case/control status
caveats: With 60 cases/60 controls and only one signature covariate, this is a hypothesis-confirming model on a pre-specified score, not a discovery model — do not add other covariates unless metadata.csv contains more than condition, time, event (it currently reports only 4 columns total)
Check the number of observed events (not just samples) before over-interpreting a marginal p-value; a low event count sharply limits power for detecting a modest hazard ratio
Confirm event coding (1=event/0=censored or the reverse) explicitly from metadata before fitting — a flipped event indicator silently inverts the hazard ratio's direction
If the proportional-hazards assumption is violated for signature_score or condition, report the violation and note that the HR is a time-averaged effect rather than a constant hazard ratio
steps.question: Once case versus control status is included as a covariate, is the 20-gene signature score independently associated with time to the recorded event in this 120-sample cohort?
acceptance_criteria: A Cox proportional-hazards model of Surv(time, event) ~ signature_score + condition is fit on all samples with complete time/event/score/condition data
Report the hazard ratio, 95% CI, and p-value for signature_score adjusted for condition, and separately for condition adjusted for signature_score
Fit and report two comparison models: signature_score alone (unadjusted) and condition alone, to show what the adjustment changes
Fit a model including a condition:signature_score interaction term and report whether it is significant, to test whether the score's prognostic effect differs between cases and controls
Proportional-hazards assumption is tested (e.g., scaled Schoenfeld residuals) for the primary adjusted model and any violation is reported, not ignored
Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by signature score (median or tertile split) are produced within each condition stratum for visualization, with log-rank test statistics reported
All effect estimates are reported with the number of events driving them (event count in the 120-sample cohort), since a small event count limits how many covariates the model can reliably support

steps.name: Cross-validated robustness check of the fixed 20-gene score against full-feature selection
caveats: This step must select features fresh inside each cross-validation fold from the full expression matrix — do not reuse the 20-gene list as a pre-filter, or the comparison to the fixed signature becomes meaningless
With ~120 samples and likely a modest number of events, cross-validated Cox concordance estimates will have wide uncertainty; report that spread rather than a single point estimate
This is a secondary/context step; the primary answer to the research question is T2S1
steps.question: Does the association between the pre-specified 20-gene score and time-to-event hold up under a properly cross-validated re-derivation of a signature from the full ~12000-gene feature space, or is the fixed panel's apparent association fragile relative to what a resampled model finds by chance in a cohort of this size?
acceptance_criteria: A cross-validated penalized Cox model (e.g., L1/elastic-net Cox) is fit on the full VST-normalized gene expression matrix (not restricted to the 20 signature genes) with time/event as outcome and condition as a forced-in covariate, using k-fold CV with feature selection performed inside each fold

The cross-validated concordance index (or partial likelihood deviance) of the full-feature model is compared against the concordance index of the fixed 20-gene score model from T2S1, both adjusted for condition
Report explicitly that this is a robustness/context check, not a claim that the full-feature model is a validated new signature — no claims of a new discovered signature are made from this step
State the achieved concordance index with a confidence interval or resampling spread, and flag if the CV performance estimate is optimistic due to the modest sample size (120) and event count

plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event, adjusted for case/control
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 60 cases vs 60 controls (single batch, unpaired) with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 121 samples incl. one extra column likely gene ID), a metadata table with condition/time/event, and a pre-specified unweighted 20-gene signature (gene symbols, no weights). The research question is explicitly about whether the signature SCORE tracks time-to-event once case/control status is held constant — this is a prognostic-adjustment question, not a discovery question, so the plan does not run genome-wide differential expression as the primary analysis. The workflow is: (1) load and QC-align counts/metadata/signature, confirm signature genes are present in the count matrix and map cleanly to gene symbols; (2) normalize the raw counts appropriately for a small non-DE quantitative-score use case (library-size + variance-stabilizing normalization via DESeq2's VST, which is standard for deriving per-sample expression values from RNA-seq counts before building a score) and compute a single per-sample signature score (mean of standardized/VST-normalized expression across the 20 genes, since no weights are supplied — an unweighted z-score composite is the only defensible choice with no weight vector); (3) fit a multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model of time-to-event ~ signature_score + case/control status, test the proportional-hazards assumption, and report the score's hazard ratio adjusted for case/control, together with an unadjusted (score-only) model and a case/control-only model for comparison, plus a case/control x score interaction term to check whether the score's prognostic effect differs by group; (4) as a secondary robustness step, evaluate whether the score's association survives a full-feature, cross-validated selection to characterize whether the fixed 20-gene panel is doing better or worse than a resampled null, and produce Kaplan-Meier stratification by score tertile/median within each case/control stratum for visualization. No DE, enrichment, or drug-repurposing steps are included because the question is narrowly a biomarker-outcome association question on a pre-specified signature, not a discovery question — enrichment/pathway reference data (WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark) available in the environment is not needed here and is not invoked speculatively.
